market_summary: Wall Street closed higher on Tuesday ahead of Nvidia: the S&P 500 rose 0.3% to 7,677, the Nasdaq 0.7% to 26,151 and semis led (SOX about +1.2%, SOXX ETF +1.6%), while the 10-year yield fell 9bp to 4.62% as WTI crude dropped 5% to ~$80.70 on signs the US is shifting to economic rather than military pressure on Iran; bitcoin briefly topped $80K before settling ~$78.8K. The Asia open looks constructive: Nikkei futures are +1.3% at ~66,170 versus Tuesday's 65,856 cash close, ASX 200 futures are +1.0% at 9,147, and the Kospi finished +0.7% on Tuesday after SK hynix reversed a 4.5% drop. On the watchlist, Robinhood (+8.2%), Bloom (+6.6%) and Sea (+6.5%) led, Broadcom (-0.6%) and GE Vernova (-1.6%) lagged, and Siemens Energy published an after-close ad-hoc confirming it will separate and deconsolidate its Transformation of Industry unit while keeping a minority stake, so Frankfurt reacts tonight AEST. Today's path: July PCE and the Q2 GDP revision at 22:30 AEST tonight, then Nvidia (consensus ~$92B revenue) and Salesforce at ~6:30am AEST Thursday, Marvell on Friday morning AEST, and Fed chair Warsh at Jackson Hole at 12am AEST Saturday; OpenAI's claim that its Broadcom-built Jalapeno chip beats Nvidia's GB300 on efficiency adds a custom-silicon subplot to the print.

AMZN.reason: Closed down 0.4% at $261.06 (flat after hours) after Monday's 1.3% gain, with the P/E near a decade low and AWS growing 37% on a $496B backlog; the reported 'Tetromino' plan for AI-automated delivery stations (2.5x throughput, pilot in 2028) is a long-dated margin lever, but the $220B capex plan, Bezos selling and state antitrust suits keep a lid on the multiple, so hold rather than chase.

AXOS.reason: Closed up 1.9% at $98.82 after announcing a dual listing on NYSE Texas, a cosmetic change; Benchmark's Aug 13 target hike to $120 (Buy) on above-peer growth and 17% ROE supports continuing to hold.

BABA.reason: The ADR closed up 0.8% at $119.44 as insiders lean in against the record HK$80B ($10.2B) placement: Jack Ma bought more than HK$600M of shares over consecutive days (SCMP) and chair Joe Tsai added another 720,000 Hong Kong shares on Tuesday, while BofA kept Buy/$172; the ~3.7% dilution and Michael Burry's exit still argue for waiting for the stock to base before adding.

ENPH.reason: Closed up 0.5% at $37.35 (slightly lower after hours) after a 3.7% drop on Aug 24 with no fundamental catalyst; the AI assistant, IQ Battery C80 and a Dutch net-metering campaign are incremental, so stay on the sidelines until residential demand stabilizes.

FIGR.reason: Jumped 6.5% to close at $41.14 (and $41.39 after hours) after EDX Markets integrated Figure's YLDS stablecoin as institutional collateral and a treasury asset, another distribution win on top of the Q2 beat (marketplace volume +132% to $4.3B) and Bernstein's $70 target; hold and let execution play out.

GOOGL.reason: Closed down 0.3% at $346.96 despite a busy day: Google Cloud launched Gemini Enterprise for Financial Services and for Legal (Moody's, Deutsche Bank, CME, Weil on board), Waymo confirmed Munich as its first EU city with public service targeted for late 2027, and Morgan Stanley argued TPUs could generate ~$200B of cloud revenue over two years; these support Cloud's +82% growth, Pixel production leaving China by 2027 trims tariff risk, and the post-Jeff-Dean dip remains a reasonable entry.

LDI.reason: Bounced 3.7% to close at $0.92 but remains below the $1 NYSE threshold after the formal non-compliance notice, with Goldman at Sell and a $1 target; exchange-compliance and dilution risk argue for reducing exposure.

META.reason: Closed up 2% at $570.05 as William Blair flagged a $100B+ opportunity in Meta's business AI agents and The Information's report that the Hatch consumer agent launches within weeks; but in the 29-state teen-addiction trial a former Instagram data scientist testified that only ~0.2% of teens ever turned on the opt-in 'take a break' reminder and that leadership rejected making it default for fear of hurting engagement metrics, and Instagram head Adam Mosseri began testifying late Tuesday. With the $942M New Mexico liability and $125-145B capex keeping the stock ~28% off its high, hold pending trial clarity.

MRVL.reason: Closed up 4.8% at $240.38 as Rosenblatt initiated at Buy with a $300 target, Susquehanna lifted its target to $265 (Wells Fargo $310 on Monday) and BofA listed it among eight 'enhanced buy' chip stocks, all citing the Google warrant deal covering roughly $120B of custom AI product business through 2033; options still imply a ~12% move on Thursday's print (Fri ~6:30am AEST) against ~$2.71B revenue and $0.93 EPS consensus, and with the stock up ~160% YTD the bar is high, so hold through the report.

MU.reason: Closed up 2.5% at $932.97, recovering part of Monday's 5.8% drop on the CXMT/YMTC-for-Apple report, which Lynx Equity called an overreaction; Mizuho trimmed its target to $1,300 from $1,375 but kept Outperform, BofA named it an 'enhanced buy' while flagging ~10% further downside risk for the SOX, Barron's argues Micron will miss part of a 50% memory-price rise because of long-term contracts, HBM remains sold out through 2027, and expect volatility through Nvidia's print.

NFLX.reason: Closed up 2.8% at $82.23 after Wolfe Research raised its target to $95 from $84 (22x 2028 EPS of $4.41), arguing Q2's soft engagement was a release-schedule issue and that returning titles set up stronger second-half results; reports that Netflix is exploring hosting Peacock and Fox One inside its own app point to a distribution-hub strategy, an ads-leadership reshuffle is worth watching but does not change the thesis, and at ~36% below the 52-week high with ad-tier and bundling optionality the valuation reset remains an add opportunity.

NVDA.reason: Closed up 2.2% at $213.05 ($213.75 after hours), snapping a seven-day losing streak, as Raymond James lifted its target to $352 and Perplexity launched a local-AI 'Portable Computer' co-developed with Nvidia for DGX Spark and RTX machines; the offsets are OpenAI's Jalapeño chip, whose SemiAnalysis benchmarks claim more throughput per kilowatt than Blackwell (volume in 2027), and Morgan Stanley credit analysts flagging ~$200B of contingent financing exposure by 2028 from Nvidia's vendor-financing of customers. Options price a ~5% (~$280B) move on Wednesday's report (Thu ~6:30am AEST) against ~$92B revenue consensus, so hold and reassess after the print.

RKT.reason: Closed up 1.5% at $14.30 as Rocket Money launched Rowan, an Anthropic-powered AI agent that cancels subscriptions, renegotiates bills and automates savings for a new Premium Plus tier, a small but real step toward monetizing the personal-finance funnel; Monday's FTC settlement of the Zillow/Redfin rental-listings case removed a legal overhang, the 10-year yield falling to 4.62% helps at the margin, but after the earlier ~50% run the shares still look fully priced, so hold.

TSM.reason: Closed up 1.8% at $417.41 after Taipei shares rebounded 1.05% to NT$2,400; Apple's new M6 is described as a 2nm chip, the first mass-market 2nm silicon from TSMC's sole-source customer, and with 40%+ 2026 growth guidance, Xiaomi's 3nm Xring and the Sony image-sensor JV underlining demand breadth, the pullback from the June high remains a buying opportunity.

STRIPE.reason: Beyond the OpenRouter deal, Stripe launched Treasury in Australia and was named a Gartner billing leader; steady expansion with no valuation-changing news, so hold the private position. Marked at 2.27x cost: latest valuation ~$159B (2026-02) vs ~$70B at entry (https://techcrunch.com/2026/02/24/stripes-valuation-soars-74-to-159-billion/).

OPENAI.reason: Head of data centers Chris Malone has left (WSJ), the fourth senior departure after Fidji Simo, Brad Lightcap and Denise Dresser ahead of a planned 2027 IPO, just as OpenAI lifts projected compute spending to ~$750B through 2030 and signs a 10GW Ohio lease backed by up to $105B of Nvidia guarantees; execution risk on the buildout rises, but Jalapeño's first benchmarks (more tokens per user and more throughput per kilowatt than Blackwell, scale deployment in 2027) are a meaningful step toward lowering its compute bill, offsetting the Alabama AG subpoena over the Hugging Face breach. Private, so hold. Marked at 5.43x cost: latest valuation ~$852B (2026-08) vs ~$157B at entry (https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/10/openai-reportedly-completed-a-7-billion-employee-tender-offer/).

headlines: NVDA closed +2.2% at $213.05, ending a seven-day slide, ahead of earnings Thu ~6:30am AEST; options imply a ~5% move.
META +2% to $570 even as an ex-data scientist testified only 0.2% of teens used Instagram's break reminder; Mosseri took the stand late Tuesday.
Anthropic will pitch IPO investors a $30T market on a $65B run-rate (WSJ); OpenAI's data-center chief Chris Malone is the fourth exec to leave.
S&P 500 +0.3%, Nasdaq +0.7% as oil fell 5% and the 10-year hit 4.62%; FIGR +6.5%, MRVL +4.8%; PCE lands 22:30 AEST tonight.
Siemens Energy ad-hoc after Xetra close: board starts legal separation of Transformation of Industry into standalone company, will deconsolidate and keep minority stake.
OpenAI says its Broadcom-co-designed Jalapeno inference chip beats Nvidia's GB300 on throughput per watt; Broadcom closes -0.6%, Robinhood +8%, Bloom +7%.
